chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-A'la ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the accidental killing, (the diyya is) one hundred camels, or one thousand sheep, or ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars. If (it is paid in) camels, then twenty-five Ibnat Makhad (one-year-old she-camels), and twenty-five Ibnat Labun (two-year-old she-camels), and twenty-five Hiqqah (three-year-old she-camels), and twenty-five Jadha'ah (four-year-old she-camels).

And the aggravated blood money for the erroneous (killing) which resembles the deliberate — that is, one who strikes with a stone or a stick, one strike or two, not intending to kill him — then it is in thirds: thirty-three Hiqqah, and thirty-three Jadha'ah, and thirty-four Thaniyyah (five-year-old she-camels), all of them being pregnant and capable of bearing the stallion. And if (it is paid in) sheep, then a thousand rams.
And (as for) the deliberate (killing), it is retaliation (qisas) or (according to) the satisfaction of the guardian of the slain.

key_terms.ابْنَة مَخَاض: one-year-old she-camel — youngest category of camel accepted in diyya
key_terms.الدِّيَة الْمُغَلَّظَة: aggravated blood money — heavier payment for quasi-intentional killing
key_terms.الْخَطَأ: accidental killing — unintentional homicide where neither act nor outcome was intended
key_terms.الْقَوَد: retaliation — retributive justice equal to the crime committed (qisas)
key_terms.حِقَّة: three-year-old she-camel — the most common category in diyya assessments
key_terms.خَلِفَة: pregnant she-camel — required for aggravated diyya, indicating higher quality
key_terms.دِيَة: blood money/wergild — financial compensation paid to the family of a killed person
key_terms.وَلِيّ الْمَقْتُول: guardian of the slain — the heir or next-of-kin who has authority over the homicide case

ai.seo_question: What are the types of blood money (diyya) for accidental and intentional killing according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the three categories of homicide in Islamic jurisprudence and their corresponding blood money (diyya) payments. For accidental killing, the standard diyya may be paid in camels of specific ages, sheep, dirhams, or dinars. For quasi-intentional killing (where the killer used a non-lethal weapon but death resulted without intent), an aggravated diyya of pregnant she-camels is required. For deliberate murder, the default is retaliation (qisas), though the victim's guardian may accept alternative compensation. The specific age categories of camels reflect the classical fiqh system for determining diyya value and quality.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’la Bin Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘With regards to the erroneous killing, it (wergild) is a hundred from the camels, or a thousand from the sheep, or ten thousand Dirhams, or a thousand Dinars. So if it was the camels, so twenty-five should be Ibnat Makhaz (two year old females), and twenty five Ibnat Laboun (three year old females), and twenty five Hiqqa (four year old females), and twenty five Jaz’a (five year old females).

And the harsh wergild regarding the erroneous (killing) is that which resembles the deliberate which he struck with the rock, or with the stick, the single strike or two strikes not intending to kill him, so it is a third being thirty-three (four year old females), and thirty-three (five year old females), and thirty-four Saniyya (six year old females), all of these being capable of bearing the stallion (mount); and if it was from the sheep, so it is a thousand rams.
And (as for) the deliberate (killing), it is the retaliation or (as per) the pleasure of the guardian of the killed one’.
